summary:
Approve. The integer-first BigInt conversion fixes the precision loss and retains overflow handling and fractional rounding. No correctness defects found; reported two non-blocking suggestions for regression coverage and an explanatory comment.

Validation: all 46 Duration tests passed. A plain-node probe passed large signed integer, overflow, equality/hash/HashSet, ordering, high-resolution time, and fractional-rounding checks. Temporary probe removed; working tree clean. Broad check/lint suites were intentionally not run, as requested.

params.title: Extend the large-value regression to equality and hashing
params.body: Could this epoch-sized value also be included in the existing Millis/Nanos equality-and-hash test? The new assertion protects `toNanosUnsafe`, but the PR also promises that a large Millis value equals its exact Nanos representation and works as the same HashSet key. The existing cross-representation hash test uses only small values (and the overflow equality assertion does not check its hash). Explicit large-value equality, equal hashes, and HashSet lookup would preserve that public contract if these paths are later refactored. This is non-blocking; the current implementation shares the helper correctly.

params.title: Cover the signed high-resolution example as well
params.body: Consider adding the large epoch example to `toHrTime`, including its negative counterpart: `[1760450000, 123000000]` and `[-1760450000, -123000000]`. The added bigint assertion covers the conversion helper, but does not directly record the user-facing high-resolution result from the PR description or its signed remainder convention. This is optional regression coverage, not a correctness issue in the current code.

params.title: Document why the fractional branch cannot overflow
params.body: A short comment explaining the removed finite-product fallback would help preserve this fix: finite non-integer doubles are necessarily below 2**52 in magnitude, so multiplying that branch by 1e6 cannot overflow; larger finite values are integers and take the exact BigInt branch. That invariant is not obvious from `Number.isInteger` alone and explains why this still covers the earlier overflow bug. Documentation only; no functional change is needed.

Validation: `pnpm test --run packages/effect/test/Duration.test.ts` passed all 46 tests. A temporary scratchpad run with plain `node` checked 10 integer inputs (positive/negative epoch values, MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, 2**1023, MAX_VALUE, and signed zero): exact nanos, Duration.equals, Equal.equals, equal hashes, HashSet lookup, and Order all passed. The scratchpad was removed.

The plain-node probe confirmed the retained overflow behavior for both signs of 2**1023 and Number.MAX_VALUE. Fractional rounding checks for ±0.0000015 ms and 1.0005 ms also passed. The targeted test file passed 46/46 tests; this comment request is only a maintainability nit.
